title: Tribute Giraffe with Attendant (later copy after Shen Du's 1414 original)
creator: after Shen Du (later Ming copy)
why_public_domain: Painting made centuries before 1929; public domain worldwide (OpenStax World History, credits it as Public Domain via Wikimedia Commons). Cropped from panel (a) of the OpenStax composite.
original_holder: holder of this copy not confirmed
caption: A later copy of the court painter Shen Du's portrait of the giraffe presented to the Yongle Emperor in 1414. Officials hailed the animal, which reached China by way of Bengal and the treasure-fleet routes, as a qilin and a sign of heaven's favour.

title: Zheng He's ships (Chinese woodblock print)
creator: Unknown Chinese woodblock artist
why_public_domain: Print made centuries before 1929; credited as Public Domain by OpenStax World History (via Wikimedia Commons). Cropped from panel (b) of the OpenStax composite.
caption: Multi-masted junks of Zheng He's fleet as a Chinese printmaker imagined them some two centuries after the voyages. The picture shows how the treasure fleets lived on in Ming memory and popular fiction.

title: Building of the Great Mosque in Samarkand (from the Zafarnama)
creator: Attributed to Kamal ud-Din Bihzad (Timurid Herat school)
why_public_domain: 15th-century manuscript painting; public domain worldwide. Credited as Public Domain by OpenStax World History (via Wikimedia Commons). Cropped from panel (b) only; panel (a) of the source composite is a modern CC BY 2.0 photograph and was NOT used.
original_holder: Garrett Zafarnama manuscript, John Work Garrett Library, Johns Hopkins University (attribution as commonly cited)
caption: Masons, stone-haulers and an elephant at work on Timur's great congregational mosque in Samarkand, painted for a later history of his campaigns. The Castilian envoy Clavijo saw this mosque rising when he reached the city in 1404.

title: Meriwether Lewis
creator: Charles Willson Peale
why_public_domain: Painted 1807; artist died 1827; public domain worldwide. Reproduced in OpenStax U.S. History Cropped from panel (a).
caption: Meriwether Lewis painted from life by Charles Willson Peale in 1807, the year after the expedition returned. Peale hung the portrait in his Philadelphia museum alongside specimens the Corps had brought back.

title: William Clark
creator: Charles Willson Peale
why_public_domain: Painted c. 1807–1810; artist died 1827; public domain worldwide. Reproduced in OpenStax U.S. History. Cropped from panel (b).
caption: William Clark, the expedition's co-captain and chief mapmaker, painted by Charles Willson Peale a few years after the journey. Clark later spent decades as the federal government's senior Indian agent in St. Louis.

title: A Map of Lewis and Clark's Track Across the Western Portion of North America
creator: Samuel Lewis (copyist) after William Clark; engraved by Samuel Harrison
why_public_domain: Published 1814; public domain worldwide. Reproduced in OpenStax U.S. History (low-resolution copy, 585 px wide).
original_holder: Published with Nicholas Biddle's 1814 History of the Expedition; copies at the Library of Congress and other libraries
caption: The 1814 map built from William Clark's field charts, tracing the route from the Mississippi up the Missouri, over the Rockies and down the Columbia to the Pacific. It replaced guesswork about the West with a measured line of rivers and ranges.

title: Lewis and Clark at Three Forks (detail)
creator: Edgar Samuel Paxson
why_public_domain: Published/installed 1912 (before 1929) and artist died 1919; public domain in the US and life+70 countries. Reproduced in OpenStax Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness, which identifies it as the Montana House of Representatives mural. Cropped from panel (a).
original_holder: Montana State Capitol, House of Representatives chamber, Helena
caption: A 1912 mural imagining Lewis, Clark and Sacagawea at the Three Forks of the Missouri in July 1805, near the place where she had been captured as a girl. No portrait of Sacagawea made in her lifetime exists, so the painter's likeness is invented.

title: A View of Matavai Bay in the Island of Otaheite
creator: William Hodges
why_public_domain: Painted 1776; artist died 1797; public domain worldwide. Full-resolution source image published by Standard Ebooks (CC0 production) as the cover source for its edition of Melville's Typee; downscaled to 2000 px wide.
original_holder: Yale Center for British Art, Paul Mellon Collection
caption: Matavai Bay on Tahiti, where the Endeavour anchored in 1769 so that Cook's party could observe the transit of Venus. William Hodges painted it after visiting with Cook's second voyage in 1773, showing Tahitian double canoes and the mountains behind the bay.
